pack.title: Compliance package
pack.notice: Downloads a compressed file (.tar.gz) to hand to an auditor. It holds the signed record this console reads, the configured policy and its digest, the attester's public keys, the SHA-256 sums of every file, and a LEEME.txt that explains how to verify it with praetore-verify without trusting this console, and what the package does not prove. If the console has execution or approver keys configured, it also holds approvals.jsonl, with the approval, rejection, expiry and execution receipts of every held request, and the execution and approver public keys that verify them. It includes the output of every executed action, which may hold sensitive data: review it before handing the package over. It holds no private keys. Downloading it changes nothing.

notice.receipt_not_authorization: This is a receipt of what already happened. It is not a current authorization, nor proof of an effect outside this record.
notice.inbox_how_it_works: Each request shows its parameters: the signature covers them. The first click shows the summary and the second signs one single decision. “Approve and execute” records the approval and asks for the single execution; if the execution cannot be done, the request stays approved, awaiting execution, and only the execution is retried. Rejecting is final. This console signs on this computer; the system records and executes.
